title: French Press Coffee with a Short Bloom and Long Steep
summary: Coarsely ground coffee steeped in hot water for 4–6 minutes, then pressed to separate the grounds, creating a rich and full-bodied brew.

steps.title: Boil
steps.text: Boil the water and let it sit 30 s, reaching about 95 °C.

steps.title: Warm
steps.text: Warm the 1000 ml press with hot water and empty it.

steps.title: Grind
steps.text: Grind the 56 g beans to a coarse consistency, between filter and very coarse.

steps.title: Bloom
steps.text: Tip the grounds into the press, pour in just enough water to wet them all and let bloom 30 s.

steps.title: Steep
steps.text: Add the rest of the 900 ml water, stir briefly, and set the lid on with the plunger raised so it does not touch the coffee; steep for 4–6 min, depending on how light or full-bodied you like it.

steps.title: Press
steps.text: Press the plunger down slowly and steadily, holding the jug; if it resists, lift slightly and press again, but do not force it.

steps.title: Pour
steps.text: Pour all the coffee out at once into mugs or a carafe so it does not keep brewing; for a cleaner brew, pour through a paper filter.

tips: Press the plunger down slowly; forcing it can cause grounds to clog and break the seal.
Pour the entire pot at once into mugs or a separate container to stop the brewing process.
safety: Each 240 ml serving contains roughly 95 mg of caffeine.
storage: Brew and serve fresh. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
